skill.name: Run-ons and fragments: make it a sentence
skill.why: Readers need to know where each thought stops. Run-ons and fragments muddle that.
skill.how: Check: who or what, what they did, makes sense alone. Two thoughts? Split or join them.

steps.say: My slime exploded! Is that a real sentence? First, find what the slime did.

show.nudge: The slime is the doer. What did it do?
That says where. What did the slime do?

steps.ask: Tap the verb. What did the slime do?
steps.win: Yes! A doer and a verb that make sense alone. That is a main clause. Every sentence needs one.

steps.say: This one has a doer and a verb too. Zed says it is a sentence. Say it alone.

options.text: Yes: it has a doer and a verb.
options.reason: It does. But say it alone: 'Because the dogs get bored.' Is it finished?

options.text: No: it leaves you waiting.
Yes: it ends with a full stop.
options.reason: A full stop alone doesn't make a sentence. Say it aloud. Is it finished?

steps.win: Right! It's only a dependent clause. A piece of a sentence like this is called a fragment.

steps.say: Hook it onto a main clause. Read the whole thing.
steps.ask: Is it a whole sentence now?

check.nudge: Read it all: 'Our dogs bark all night because they get bored.' Does it leave you waiting?

steps.win: Yes! The because part hangs on the main clause. Now it is one whole sentence.

steps.say: Here's another fragment. What's missing this time?

options.text: a doer and a verb
a joining word
options.reason: A joining word won't fix it. Who did something here? What did they do?

options.text: nothing, it is a sentence
options.reason: Say it alone: 'Under the jetty.' Who did what?

steps.win: Right! It only says where. Add a doer and a verb: 'A crab hid under the jetty.'

steps.say: Careful! An -ing word looks like a verb, but it cannot be the verb by itself.

options.text: A crab hiding under the jetty!
options.reason: An exclamation mark won't fix it. 'Hiding' still needs a helper word.

options.text: A crab, hiding under the jetty.
options.reason: A comma won't fix it. 'Hiding' needs a word like 'was' in front.

options.text: A crab was hiding under the jetty.

steps.win: Yes! 'Was hiding' works. An -ing word needs was, were, is or am to be the verb.

steps.say: Each main clause is a complete thought. Two jammed together with nothing between them make a run-on.

show.nudge: That has one main clause and a full stop. It is a whole sentence.

show.text: The slime exploded it went everywhere.

show.nudge: No doer, no verb. That is a fragment.

steps.win: Yes! Two main clauses are jammed together with nothing between. Fix it with a full stop after exploded.

steps.say: Gus put a comma in. A comma alone cannot join two main clauses.

options.text: The slime exploded it went everywhere.
options.reason: Now there's nothing between the clauses. That's a run-on again.

options.text: The slime exploded, and it went everywhere.
The slime exploded, it went everywhere!
options.reason: An exclamation mark won't fix it. There's still only a comma between the clauses.

steps.win: Yes! A comma plus a joining word like 'and', 'but' or 'so' can join two main clauses.

terms.means: A doer and a verb that make sense alone. Every sentence needs one.
Only a piece: no doer, no verb, or no main clause. 'Under the jetty.'
Two main clauses with nothing, or only a comma, between them.
Goes after the comma to join two main clauses: 'and', 'but', 'so'.

card.test: Find the main clause. None? Fragment. Two with nothing between? Run-on. Split or join them.

weDo.prompt: Which one is a complete sentence?
weDo.hint: A complete sentence has a doer and a verb that make sense alone, with nothing jammed on.
weDo.success: 'Gus sneezed into the slime.' It says who and what he did, and it's one complete thought.

options.text: Gus sneezed into the slime.
Sneezing into the slime.
options.reason: This is a fragment. Who was sneezing? It doesn't say.

options.text: Gus sneezed into the slime it turned green.
options.reason: This is a run-on. Two complete thoughts are jammed together with nothing between them.

weDo.text: The bus was late we missed the start of the movie.
weDo.hint: Two complete thoughts need a full stop between them, or a comma and a joining word.
weDo.success: A comma plus 'so' joins the two thoughts properly and shows that one caused the other.

options.text: The bus was late, so we missed the start of the movie.
The bus was late, we missed the start of the movie.
options.reason: A comma alone can't hold two complete thoughts together. What else could go with the comma?

options.text: Because the bus was late. We missed the start of the movie.
options.reason: 'Because the bus was late.' is a fragment. It leaves you waiting for what happened.
